t: Montgomery planned a battle of attrition in which his superiority in men, tanks, guns and aircraft would 'crumble' the Axis defences; he expected it to last 12 days, and it lasted 13.

Axis fuel was short throughout: by 25 October Panzerarmee Afrika had three days' supply, only two days' of it east of Tobruk, and tankers carrying fuel were sunk at the end of October and in early November.

Casualty figures differ by source: Eighth Army lost 13,560 men, while Axis losses are put at 36,939 in one reckoning that Niall Barr calls very uncertain, and as much larger totals once the retreat is counted.
dyk: Before the attack Eighth Army hid its build-up in the north with dummy dumps under camouflage nets, dummy tanks and guns of calico and palm-frond hurdles in the south, real tanks disguised as trucks with plywood superstructures, and a dummy water pipeline built slowly enough to suggest it would not be finished until after the attack.
ev: Panzer Army Africa wins the Battle of Gazala and advances into Egypt
Axis attacks in the First Battle of El Alamein are defeated
Churchill and Brooke replace Auchinleck with Alexander, and Montgomery takes command of Eighth Army
Rommel's attack is repulsed at the Alam el Halfa ridge
Operation Lightfoot opens with a barrage of 1,000 guns
Operation Supercharge begins, and the 9th Armoured Brigade attacks the Axis gun line; on 4 November the Axis front is broken and Rommel orders a retreat
Eighth Army takes Tripoli as Rommel withdraws to the Mareth Line

f.date: 23 October – 4 November 1942 (a 13-day battle; the Axis retreat and the Allied pursuit continued to 11 November)
f.place: Near the railway halt of El Alamein on the Mediterranean coast of Egypt, on a front between the sea and the Qattara Depression, about 50 miles (80 km) from Alexandria
f.sides: The British Commonwealth Eighth Army under Lieutenant-General Bernard Montgomery, with 195,000 men and 1,029 tanks; the German-Italian Panzer Army (Panzerarmee Afrika) under Field Marshal Erwin Rommel, with 116,000 men and 547 tanks
f.outcome: The Axis defences were broken and Panzerarmee Afrika was forced to retreat from Egypt and Libya; most of the Italian infantry, which lacked transport, was abandoned. The victory ended the Axis threat to the Middle East and Iran.
